prompt.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: a THREE-FRAME limited-animation key-pose SPRITE SHEET of this exact Song dynasty village woman sitting low on the ground re-binding the head of a long-handled farm tool in front of a shed, seen from the same slightly high three-quarter angle as the reference. Keep her identity: black double hair bun with a small ornament, pale blue-grey jacket with cream cuffs, lavender-grey trousers, and the SAME small woven basket on the ground beside her. THE TOOL IS ONE PIECE IN EVERY CELL: a long straight wooden handle with a curved iron blade FIRMLY FIXED to its upper end, the blade and handle joined by a wrapping of brown cord. The blade is ALWAYS attached to the handle in all three cells. Never draw a loose or separate blade, never draw a second blade, nothing lies on the ground except the basket. She stays sitting in exactly the same place in all three cells; her legs, hips and the basket do not move; only her arms, hands, head and the tool move. Cell 1 (left) = rest: the tool lies diagonally across her knees, the bladed end to the right of the image resting just above the basket, she looks down at the cord wrapping at the joint. Cell 2 (middle) = binding: the tool in the same place across her knees, she winds the brown cord tightly around the joint just below the blade with both hands, the free end of the cord pulled out to the right. Cell 3 (right) = checking: she lifts the whole tool up in front of her with both hands, blade end raised above her head to the right, and looks along the edge, back straight; the cord wrapping is now neat and tight. Fine ink outlines and muted antique Chinese watercolor exactly matching the reference, same line weight, same palette, same paper-grain shading. Truly transparent alpha background, no ground shadow, no glow, no grid lines, no numbers, no text. One single horizontal row of 3 equal-width cells, one full figure per cell, centered in its cell with generous margin so the raised blade, the handle end, the cord and the basket never touch a cell edge. Identical character size and identical camera angle in every cell. Redraw at higher detail than the small reference without changing the design. Make every cell match the reference figure and match each other as strictly as possible.

note: v2: v1 drew the blade loose on the ground in cells 1-2 and fixed on the handle in cell 3.
